title: A Sincere Suggestion: Adding an AI Interface to Enhance Reading and Discussion on Your E-Book App
text:
As a loyal user of your e-book app for over two years, I’ve always admired how it makes reading more accessible—whether I’m diving into a classic novel during my commute or studying a nonfiction book on weekends, its clean interface and vast library have turned reading into a daily joy. Yet lately, I’ve noticed a small but meaningful gap in my experience, one that I believe an AI interface could beautifully fill.

Like many readers, I don’t just read to “finish” a book—I read to understand it, to unpack its ideas, and to bounce thoughts off someone when a passage feels confusing or inspiring. There have been countless times when I’ve hit a wall: when I struggled to grasp the metaphor in a poem by Emily Dickinson, when the technical jargon in a science book left me stuck, or even when I wanted to debate the choices of a novel’s protagonist but had no one to share those thoughts with (my friends, sadly, aren’t as obsessed with literary twists as I am). In those moments, I wished my e-book app could do more than just display text—it could be a “reading companion” that meets me where I am.

That’s why I’m writing to suggest adding an AI interface to your app: one designed to discuss books with readers and help unpack tricky content. Imagine this: while reading 1984, I could ask the AI, “Why does Orwell use the phrase ‘doublethink’—how does it reflect the novel’s message?” And instead of scrolling through endless online forums (which often feel unfocused), the AI would respond in a conversational way, linking the phrase to the story’s themes without giving away too much. For nonfiction, it could break down complex concepts—like explaining economic theories in a business book using simple examples, or clarifying the historical context of a memoir—so I don’t have to pause reading to look up definitions elsewhere.

What makes this idea special, I think, is that it wouldn’t replace human discussion—it would complement it. For readers who live alone, have busy schedules, or just prefer quiet, independent reading, the AI would be a constant, non-intimidating partner. It could even adapt to how I read: if I’m a casual reader, it would keep explanations light; if I’m a student digging deeper for an essay, it could offer more detailed analysis. Most of all, it would turn reading from a solitary act into a more engaging, enriching process—something that aligns perfectly with what your app already does so well: making books feel alive.

I know adding new features takes time and effort, and I deeply appreciate all the work your team puts into making this app a favorite for so many of us. But I truly believe an AI reading companion would make your app stand out even more—not just as a tool for accessing books, but as a tool for connecting with them.

Thank you for taking the time to read this suggestion. I’ll keep using and loving your app either way, but I can’t help but hope to one day have that little “AI chat” button pop up on my screen—ready to talk books with me, one confusing (or wonderful) passage at a time.

Sincerely,
A Grateful Reader
